name: manual_67540d
claim: Self-reflection: when a user's fix instruction could reasonably be read as either instance-specific or class-general, default to checking for the general case BEFORE presenting the narrow fix as done, rather than shipping the narrow fix and waiting for the user to ask 2-3 more times to broaden it.

decisions.notes: This session's skill-naming collision fix took three user prompts to reach its final, correct scope: first a narrow CI-identity-secret fix, then 'cross-reference all skills', then 'generalize the mechanism in both'. Each was the right next question for the user to ask, but a more proactive first pass -- checking the full manifest for other collisions and proposing a shared mechanism up front, once the first instance revealed the bug class existed -- would have reached the same correct endpoint in one turn instead of three. Not every fix needs this (most really are instance-specific), but a fix that stems from 'I found a bug in how X is checked' is a signal worth pausing on before declaring done.
